suite: dead-code-deletion (migration shims and obsolete interchange formats)

findings.rationale: Pure documentation module with no runtime items. Compiler-checked intra-doc links serve as the authoritative removal ledger for legacy structs still retained pending F1.5/F3 cutover. The module explicitly lists what gates will remove which types. It is not dead code — it is the anti-drift safety net.

The legacy VectorStore impl (targeting `mem_vectors`, migration 0002) is still actively called by: write_policy/slow.rs (F3.1 write path), Lifecycle module (deletion residue), and memory_graph_v2.rs integration tests (lc_seed / seed_ns_pair helpers). The `cosine()` wrapper is called directly from the legacy `VectorStore::search` impl (line 869 of sqlite_vectors.rs). Both are retained pending the F3.1 write-path cutover explicitly documented in the source header. Not dead code.

LEGACY_TABLES is a live allow-list used by `reconciliation_report()` to count legacy rows before a hard reset. It is defensive reporting infrastructure (count-if-exists guards), not a compatibility shim. It reads but never writes or deletes.

The comment `// Legacy relationships table dropped; v2 edge reads land in F3.3.` is an inline documentation note explaining why graph_relationships() returns Vec::new(). It is accurate and not dead code.

This is the CURRENT V-IO-01 canonical interchange format (v1.0). There is no old/superseded interchange format alongside it. `InterchangeVersion::v1()` IS the current version. The version compatibility logic (major version match, minor backward-compat) is the live policy for round-trip semantics, not a legacy shim.

Despite the `_compat` in its name, migration 0005 creates memory_facts, snippets, and document_chunks tables that are actively used by runtime_backend.rs (live write/read paths) and tools/knowledge.rs (list_snippets tool). These are live production tables, not dead schema.

The migration runner is the live schema upgrade engine. All legacy-related comments are accurate transition documentation (e.g. notes that `events` coexists until F1.5 cutover). No dead code in the runner itself.

conclusion: Clean-bill-of-health scan. Zero migration compatibility shims, zero obsolete interchange format handlers, and zero dead-code markers of the targeted categories (TODO: remove after migration, COMPAT:, DEPRECATED:, legacy shim paths) were found in the memory/interchange/migration code area. All legacy-labelled constructs are either: (a) live code retained intentionally pending a documented future cutover gate (F1.5, F3, F3.1), (b) documentation-only ledger modules with no runtime items, or (c) active production tables/tools. The codebase has already completed the F2.2.7 hard cutover (LegacyRelationshipMigrator deleted, relationships table dropped via migration 0024, Rust callers removed). No further deletions are warranted at this stage.
